question: Why did the error rate go up on 21 March 2026?

contributing_factors.description: Upstream service catalog-db is experiencing degraded performance, causing errors in the catalog service.
why_chain: The catalog service is dependent on the catalog-db service.
The catalog-db service is experiencing degraded performance, leading to HTTP 503 errors.
These errors are propagated to the catalog service, causing an increase in error rate.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in error rate is due to a sudden increase in user traffic.
ruled_out.reason: The request volume for the service catalog did not change significantly.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in error rate is due to configuration changes in the catalog service.
ruled_out.reason: There is no evidence of configuration changes that would explain the sudden jump in error rate.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The catalog service deployment introduced a new version that may have introduced bugs or performance issues.
ruled_out.reason: It rests on a change that is too early, or in a different service/region, to explain a sudden change here.

evidence.summary: Error rate for service catalog rose from 0.42% to 5.47% (+1217%), with a change point at 2026-03-21T15:30:00Z.
The change is concentrated in service catalog: 3 of 12 service/region segments changed; the other segments stayed flat (largest after/before ratio 1.06).
At the same time, request volume for service catalog stayed about the same (1704 per 5 min before, 1901 per 5 min after, +12%).
At the same time, p95 latency for service catalog rose (120 ms before, 216 ms after, +80%).
Upstream catalog-db returning HTTP 503 for catalog (catalog; 2 min after the change; record R017; fit: right time and place: a strong candidate cause)
catalog: ERROR upstream catalog-db timeout after 3 retries (catalog, eu-west; 7 min after the change; record R018; fit: after the change, so a symptom, not a cause)
catalog: ERROR upstream catalog-db timeout after 3 retries (catalog, us-east; 17 min after the change; record R019; fit: after the change, so a symptom, not a cause)
Deployed catalog v3.27 to eu-west (catalog, eu-west; 224 min before the change; record R014; fit: hours before the change, too early to explain a sudden jump)
catalog-db status page: investigating degraded performance (catalog; 30 min after the change; record R021; fit: after the change, so a symptom, not a cause)

reasons: ✓ A change event (alerts) lines up in time (2 min after the change).
✓ 3 log/alert record(s) after the change agree with the numbers.
✓ Request volume stayed steady, ruling out a traffic spike.
✓ No competing change event fits as well.
✓ The main factor rests on this event.

actions.action: Investigate and fix the issue with the upstream catalog-db service.
